_meta.purpose: Step 6, Issue 4 — proves the table-scope rule in src/nl2sql/pipeline/guard.py. A candidate must stay within its tagged db's tables (single-db per run); a query touching a table outside the per-db allowed set is rejected pre-execution. Deferred from Step 4 until the schema metadata defining 'allowed' existed.
_meta.format: Adds an 'allowed_tables' field (the per-db allowed set) alongside the usual 'sql' / 'expected_verdict' / 'expected_rule'. Cases without 'allowed_tables' leave table-scope unenforced (the naive-dump path); those exercise the schema-free rules only.
_meta.rule: Deterministic sqlglot AST — base table names vs the allowed set, case-insensitive, CTE names excluded (a WITH reference is not a base table). No regex, no LLM.

cases.description: A query joining a table the db doesn't have (here an injected 'secrets' table) is rejected before execution — a hallucinated or cross-db reference.
cases.sql: SELECT u.name, s.token FROM users u JOIN secrets s ON s.user_id = u.id

cases.description: A standalone read of a table outside the allowed set is rejected.
A query touching only allowed tables passes — table-scope must not over-block legitimate in-db joins.
cases.sql: SELECT u.name, t.amount FROM users u JOIN transactions t ON t.user_id = u.id

cases.description: Table-name matching is case-insensitive: a candidate using a different case than the allowed set still passes (bounded query, so the cost rule stays out of it).
cases.sql: SELECT name FROM Users WHERE id = 1

cases.description: A CTE name is not a base table, so it must not be judged out-of-scope even though it isn't in the allowed set.
cases.sql: WITH recent AS (SELECT id FROM transactions WHERE amount > 0) SELECT id FROM recent

cases.description: A write to an out-of-scope table is caught by read-only first (rules run before table-scope, fail-fast) — precedence is deterministic.
